profile_text.body:
Cerence Inc. is a public company headquartered in Burlington, Massachusetts, traded under the ticker CRNC and registered with the SEC under CIK 0001768267. On its own site the company describes itself as delivering conversational and agentic AI-powered user experiences for automotive and beyond, powered by CaLLM, which it describes as its family of language models. It also describes the Cerence SDK V9 as delivering on-device voice AI with modular APIs, robust audio handling, and enterprise-ready security, and promotes AI Box architectures for agentic in-car experiences at the edge without disrupting existing infotainment platforms.

The site reports second quarter fiscal year 2026 results: $64.2 million in revenue, $7.2 million in Adjusted EBITDA, net income of $1.7 million, $14.1 million in operating cash flow, and $13.6 million in free cash flow. It says Cerence xUI-powered vehicles have started production and that adoption of Audio AI and generative AI solutions is expanding with global OEMs. The company says it received the ECARX 2026 Quality Pioneer Award at ECARX's Global Partner Conference for the third consecutive year, describing a partnership with ECARX dating to 2017 covering multilingual speech recognition, AI-powered voice assistants, and intelligent cockpit experiences across GEELY brands including Proton, smart Automobile, Group Lotus, and Lynk & Co. It also says it will join partner Code Factory S.L. at the National Restaurant Association Show to demo VoiceLaier, an embedded voice AI solution for self-service kiosks, with Sai Yagnyamurthy and Mi Yu from Cerence AI taking part.

The site states that Cerence built compliance with EU AI Act Article 50(2) transparency requirements for synthetic audio into its TTS product, using machine-readable metadata and digital audio watermarking across cloud and embedded environments, ahead of obligations expected to apply from August 2, 2026. Markus Funk, described as Director of User Experience at Cerence AI, is quoted in a Q&A on AI-driven design workflows. No products are tracked in the held record, and no lawsuits or MCP servers are listed.
